why: The student correctly links the unbraced else to the inner if inside the failed outer if, which explains why the first statement prints nothing for t = 5; the answer of nothing at all is correct, though the student does not explain the else-if chain.

concepts.quote: the else is part of the inner if
concepts.why: The student correctly sees that the else is a branch of the inner if, inside the outer if's then branch, and is not a second branch of the outer if.

concepts.quote: the outer if fails and the else is part of the inner if
concepts.why: The student applies the dangling-else rule correctly: without braces, the else belongs to the inner if, so when the outer test fails, neither hot nor cold is printed.
The student says nothing about assignment.
This point is covered under the nested conditionals concept.
The student does not reason about the else-if chain.
The student makes no claim about how output works.
The code has no empty statement and the student does not mention one.
The student makes no claim about statements in general.
